Hi Nina — thanks for the clear list. Quick recap + a worked example below. I'm attaching a one-pager and the spreadsheet with the same math so you can drop in your sheet.

Short answers up front:
- Recommended hit-rate assumptions (prefix/prefetch layer): conservative 15%, expected 30%, optimistic 50% — depends on prompt standardization and session stickiness.
- Effective $/1M tokens: we show both raw list price and an "effective" price after cache (i.e., external tokens * (1 - hit_rate)). For procurement SOWs we usually recommend showing the list price and an illustrative effective price at the expected hit rate (30%).

Worked example (simple):
- Baseline model list price (reference for commercial discussion): $800 per 1M tokens (this is the published unit in our quote for the LLM tier you saw).
- Raw monthly usage (example from your forecast sheet): 5,000,000 consumer-generated tokens/month.
- Cache hit rate assumption: 30% (expected) -> model-attended tokens = 5,000,000 * (1 - 0.30) = 3,500,000 tokens.
- Effective cost to you (model price * attended tokens / 1,000,000): $800 * 3.5 = $2,800 effective per million 'gross' tokens consumed. To express as $/1M gross tokens, we compute: (cost for attended tokens / gross tokens) * 1,000,000 => ($2,800 / 5,000,000) * 1,000,000 = $560 per 1M gross tokens. So:
  - List price: $800 / 1M tokens
  - Effective after 30% hit: $560 / 1M gross tokens (your procurement-facing metric)

Notes and levers:
- Increasing hit rate to 50% => effective cost ~$400 / 1M gross; down to 15% => ~$680 / 1M gross.
- Prefetching more prompts (higher prefix coverage) gives diminishing returns; quality of dedup and canonicalization matters more than sheer prefetch volume.
- We recommend modeling three rows in the SOW: conservative/expected/optimistic hit rates with the corresponding effective $/1M numbers.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura (cc) will plug your uploaded forecast into our template and return a tab with conservative/expected/optimistic scenarios.
2) Monica will outline the implementation window and early pilot rules (days-to-live for the prefix cache, invalidation rules).
3) If procurement is ready, we can produce an illustrative commercial with those three price lines for the SOW.

I attached: 1-page worked example and the spreadsheet you can drop numbers into. If that looks good I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up to walk procurement through the math.

Best,

Nina — I dropped your forecast into our template and attached the worked tabs. Quick highlights from the spreadsheet I uploaded:

- Your forecast baseline: monthly gross tokens = 5M; token mix: 65% short (<=64 tokens), 35% long (>256 tokens). Short form tends to benefit more from prefix caching.
- With prefix coverage of 40% (i.e., 40% of short queries match a cached prefix), end-to-end hit rate ~28% (we model session affinity + canonicalization loss).
- Under your traffic mix and an assumed list price of $800/1M, effective procurement-number = $580 / 1M gross tokens (very close to Markus' summary; small differences due to rounding and per-request rounding to nearest 1k on our billing ingestion).

Implementation note for your engineers: we recommend starting with a 30-day pilot using a 30% hit assumption and instrumenting prefix-match ratio and canonicalization misses. We'll provide the dashboard query for the prefix-match metric in the Console.

I've attached the updated forecast with three scenarios and a short slide that maps the SLOs we'll set during the pilot. Happy to hop on the procurement call next week if you'd like.
